newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville Power lowers peak demand prices.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville Power lowers peak demand prices.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration reduced its prices for next-day power during peak demand hours, but increased off-peak prices for Northwest deliveries, the federal agency said Wednesday.
Bonneville offered firm delivered power in the Northwest between hours 0700 and 2200 PDT at $18.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), down from $19.54 for Wednesday pre-schedulings.
Firm power during the same hours delivered at the California-Oregon (COB) and Nevada-Oregon (NOB) borders was offered at $20.50 per MWh, down from $22.00.
Firm COB/NOB volumes, however, were limited to 300 MWh during peak hours.

Bonneville prices for firm power during off-peak hours at COB/NOB were unchanged at $16.00 to $18.00, but were increased for Northwest deliveries to $16.00 to $18.00 from $13.54 to $15.54 for Wednesday pre-schedulings.
BPA's changes to non-firm Thursday prices were along the same pattern: higher during peak-demand hours and lower for Northwest deliveries during light-load hours.
